doc.title: Jack DeJohnette interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 7, 2025

title: Technology in the studio and AI
summary: He says tools are fine but humans make the music.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: Well it’s nice to know the system finally worked in that technology moves so quickly, do you think that composers and players these days write differently because of what’s possible in the recording studio with all the things you can do digitally and if someone’s a bit off it’s very fixable. I guess I’m just generally asking you how you feel about the state of technology in the music world?

It’s fine. The creative aspect of it depends on the musician. You can go out as far as you want to go, or be as organized as you want. You know the tools are there, it’s the humans that make the difference. You know it’s the humans that turn out the music, not an AI machine.
